In 2024, CMS issued regulations requiring hospitals participating in federal payment programs to screen all patients for five social determinants: food insecurity, housing instability, transportation needs, utility difficulties, and interpersonal safety. These screening requirements create a standardized data foundation that could eventually support more rigorous social risk adjustment.

In 2024, CMS began requiring hospitals in its Inpatient Quality Reporting program to report screening of adult patients for five social determinants: food insecurity, housing instability, transportation needs, utility difficulties, and interpersonal safety. CMS then removed those screening measures in its FY2026 inpatient payment rule (August 2025), citing reporting burden, so the standardized federal data foundation they promised did not materialize.

For Medicare Advantage, CMS finalized a Health Equity Index (HEI) for the Star Ratings, planned for the 2027 star ratings based on 2024–2025 performance data, but cancelled it in its Contract Year 2027 final rule (April 2026) before it took effect.
